lessons.statement: A prompt-only capability patch (a0b53e13..., +24 lines of test-immutability and full-output-verification rules in instructions.md and opencode-src/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/default.txt) produced no strict matched-valid improvement: matched train aggregate fell from 0.5 to 0.375, the sole score change being a regression on NodeBB (1.0 before -> 0.0 after), and the development gate declined it with reason 'no strict matched-valid improvement'. Prompt text urging the frozen target model not to weaken tests and to re-run verification did not rescue any previously failing case.

The matched comparison is one run per case per candidate, so the single NodeBB regression (1.0 -> 0.0) and the unchanged outcomes elsewhere cannot be attributed to the prompt change with confidence; per protocol this is variability-compatible, not a demonstrated source effect. Future candidates should not treat a one-case matched delta (in either direction) as proof of a mechanism, and acceptance remains gated on strict matched-valid improvement.

The lessons store (.autosaddler/history/lessons.json) was empty before this reflection; this is the first evidence-grounded record for this lineage. The working parent remains the accepted baseline beefdebde... (dev aggregate 0.1875, no changed units), and the rejected child a0b53e13... must not be built upon as if accepted.

Both attempted children of the accepted baseline were declined for 'no strict matched-valid improvement' even though each had a plausible mechanism: prompt-only test-integrity additions (a0b53e13) went 0.5 -> 0.375 on its batch, and source-level self-verification (af51ffcf) went 0.5 -> 0.25 on the current batch. Under one-run-per-case matched comparison on 8 cases, a single 1.0 -> 0.0 flip swings the aggregate by 0.125, so declined outcomes here do not establish that the mechanisms hurt; they establish only that improvement was not demonstrated.

The recurring observed failure mode in train transcripts is premature completion: the agent edits files and declares the task done without running the project's test suite (NodeBB and ansible cases). This motivated the test-guard mechanism (tool/test-guard.ts plus edit-tool output reminders and prompt.ts self-verify injection) in af51ffcf. However, the two cases the mechanism plausibly targeted for recovery (ansible-d62496, element-web-ecfd1736) regressed 1.0 -> 0.0 under the candidate, and the previously-passing qutebrowser cases stayed 1.0, so the mechanism neither demonstrably fixed the failure mode nor demonstrably preserved passing behavior; its net effect is unproven under one-run matching.

Regression risk concentrates in cases the parent solved at 1.0: af51ffcf lost exactly the two 1.0-before cases that were not qutebrowser (ansible-d62496 1.0 -> 0.0, element-web-ecfd1736 1.0 -> 0.0) while all 0-before cases stayed 0 and both qutebrowser cases stayed 1.0. Any future change should be evaluated first against whether it can plausibly perturb currently-passing cases, since the gate requires strict improvement and losses on passing cases cannot be offset by gains on failing ones unless failures actually flip.

Local verification for af51ffcf was limited to offline compilation (autoharness-build-check.py passed) plus smoke test; no benchmark score evidence existed pre-gate. Compilation success and mechanism plausibility did not predict matched-outcome improvement. Future candidates should be designed so their mechanism is either verifiable locally against the actual failure transcripts (e.g. by replaying the recorded failing traces) or so conservative that perturbation of passing cases is unlikely; otherwise the one-run matched gate remains a coin flip on 8 cases.

Rejected candidates must not become parent code: the accepted parent remains the baseline beefdebde (iteration 0, development_aggregate 0.1875, no changed units); both a0b53e13 and af51ffcf were declined and their diffs (7bbfb8ed..., d05869f9...) are evidence of attempts, not of effective mechanisms. The next iteration must build from beefdebde's tree and treat the test-guard source changes as unproven, not as a foundation to extend blindly.

Candidate b9409991 (ripgrep fallback + error-cause surfacing in opencode-src/packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts and ripgrep/binary.ts) was declined for no strict matched-valid improvement: train aggregate stayed 0.75 -> 0.75 despite one matched gain (qutebrowser-6dd402c 0.0 -> 1.0) and one matched loss (vuls-4b680b 1.0 -> 0.0), with the other six cases unchanged. One run per case per candidate means these single-case deltas in both directions are variability-compatible and cannot be attributed to the source change; acceptance remains gated on strict matched-valid improvement, and future candidates should not treat a cancelling gain/loss pair as a mechanism demonstration.

Fixing a pervasive tool-infrastructure failure (parent evidence showed 19/19 grep and 3/3 glob calls failing with the generic 'ripgrep execution failed', while bash rg/grep/find succeeded) did not shift the matched aggregate: 5 of 8 cases already scored 1.0 before the fix and stayed 1.0, and element-web-44b9 remained 0.0. The declined diagnosis was only a hypothesis (runtime reproduction was declined), so the PATH/resolution-mismatch cause was never demonstrated. Lesson: an observed universal tool failure is not necessarily the binding constraint on task outcomes, and an undemonstrated root-cause hypothesis should be labeled as such; verify the mechanism at runtime before claiming the fix addresses it.

The working parent remains the accepted baseline beefdebde (dev aggregate 0.1875); the three attempted children a0b53e13 (prompt-only), af51ffcf (test-guard/self-verify source changes) and b9409991 (ripgrep fallback) were all declined for no strict matched-valid improvement and must not be built upon as if accepted. This reflection records the iteration-2 evidence-grounded lessons for this lineage using only current-batch case IDs.

Enforcing test integrity at the tool layer (guard in opencode-src/packages/opencode/src/tool/test-integrity.ts wired into edit.ts, write.ts and apply_patch.ts, blocking non-additive modification of tracked test files relative to git HEAD) produced the only accepted candidate (0e3d5ac2, iteration 3): matched aggregate improved 0.375->0.5 with no matched regressions, driven by qutebrowser-0b621cb 0.0->1.0 while all other 7 cases were unchanged. The same batch's failure diagnoses show 5 of 8 failures involved tampering with official tests (running wrong test names, rewriting test functions, editing official test files, or running zero unit tests), which is exactly the failure mode this guard blocks; the 3 passing cases made only additive test edits.

Prompt-level instruction additions and synthetic self-verify turns are exhausted as a mechanism: the prompt-plus-warning candidate a0b53e13 (iteration 0) was declined with matched aggregate 0.5->0.375, its sole matched change being a NodeBB regression 1.0->0.0, and prior prompt-only children (4607715e, 7bbfb8ed, d05869f9, fb1bc240) were all declined. Prompt text cannot reliably prevent official-test tampering; source-level tool enforcement was required.

With one run per case per candidate, a single-case score flip is variability-compatible and the gate is decided by matched aggregate direction and absence of matched regressions: iteration 0's only matched delta was a regression (NodeBB 1.0->0.0) and was declined, while iteration 3's only matched delta was an improvement (qutebrowser-0b621cb 0.0->1.0, all others unchanged) and was accepted as a strict matched-valid improvement. Future candidates should preserve already-passing cases and seek improvements on currently-failing tampering cases.

lessons.scope: tool reliability and error transparency (grep/glob code search)
lessons.statement: Observed in the train batch for iteration 0004: every one of the 31 grep/glob invocations across all 8 train cases failed with the identical opaque message 'ripgrep execution failed' (33 occurrences in training_evidence.json), independent of input pattern or path, and the 6 cases that stayed at score 0 (both qutebrowser and element-web cases that failed all searches were near-miss implementations). The generic wrap in packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts:146-150 discards the underlying native error, so the true training-runtime cause (hypothesis: unusable or missing rg binary / offline download failure; not demonstrated and not reproducible in the dev container) could not be confirmed from evidence. Lesson: preserve and surface the native error detail in tool failure messages so environment-dependent search failures are diagnosable, and consider a graceful degradation path when the ripgrep binary is unavailable.

Observed: iteration 0004 was accepted via strict matched-valid improvement (train before 0.25 -> after 0.375, 8 matched cases). The accepted candidate sha256:4a2c6cb5 (steering phase, +95 lines: edits to tool/apply_patch.ts, tool/edit.ts, tool/write.ts and new tool/test-integrity.ts) built on accepted parent sha256:0e3d5ac (compaction.ts context-handling change, +28 lines, accepted at iteration 0002 with train aggregate 0.25 and parent dev aggregate 0.3125). The only per-case flip was element-web-ecfd 0->1 while qutebrowser-44e64199 and qutebrowser-8f46ba3f held at 1.0 with no regressions on the remaining 5 cases. Lesson: stacking a small context-handling fix with tool-output/integrity improvements produced the sole matched gain of the batch without regressions; the specific causal component within the 4a2c6cb5 diff is not isolated by this evidence.

Observed in training evidence and prior-batch diagnoses on this case set: element-web-1077729a and NodeBB-8168c6c4 produced empty file snapshots, and the iteration-0001 diagnosis recorded the agent editing files and declaring completion without running the project's test suite (310/311 official tests unexecuted). These cases remained at 0.0 before and after the accepted 0004 patch. The accepted 4a2c6cb5 candidate introduced tool/test-integrity.ts to gate completion on verification, but no train score movement on these two cases demonstrates its effect yet. Lesson: cases with empty snapshots and unexecuted tests are a distinct, unresolved failure mode from search-tool failure; keep verification-gating and snapshot-completeness work as candidate directions for the next iteration.

The dominant failure mode on this batch is the agent treating a green run of the repository's pre-existing test suite as task completion: in element-web-44b98896 it never edited the component under test, in qutebrowser-6dd402c it replaced the repo's pytest suite with ad-hoc /tmp scripts, and in vuls-4b680b99 it appended tests that misread TestParsePkgInfo. Candidate changes should force the agent to both make the requested edit and validate it with a test tied to the new behavior, not merely observe a passing baseline suite.

The iteration-0005 shell.ts change (candidate 54e69a5, steering phase) was accepted with strict matched-valid improvement: matched train aggregate rose 0.625 to 0.875 with qutebrowser-6dd402c and vuls-4b680b99 flipping 0.0 to 1.0 while all five previously passing cases stayed at 1.0; element-web-44b98896 stayed 0.0 and remains the only failing case, so its failure (never editing the tested component) is not fixed by tool-execution-level changes alone.

The iteration-0002 ripgrep fallback fix (candidate b9409991, changed opencode-src ripgrep.ts and ripgrep/binary.ts) was declined: matched aggregate stayed 0.75 with offsetting single-case deltas (qutebrowser-6dd402c 0.0 to 1.0, vuls-4b680b99 1.0 to 0.0). With one run per case, offsetting single-case deltas are matched-outcome variability, not a demonstrated source effect, and do not meet the strict matched-valid improvement bar.
